svg.text: Proximity Service — End-to-End Architecture (100M DAU · 200M POIs · ~5,787 Avg / ~28.9k Peak QPS)
Read-Heavy Stateless LBS · 9-Cell Geohash / Adaptive Quadtree · Two-Tier Valkey Cache · Multi-Region Replicas
1. Client & L7 Routing
Mobile / Web Search Clients
GET /v1/search/nearby
&radius=500 (500M searches/day)
GET /v1/businesses/{id}
Business Owner Portal
POST / PUT / DELETE
/v1/businesses/{id}
Low write rate (~100 QPS)
Daily / CDC index refresh
GeoDNS + L7 Load Balancer
• Routes /v1/search/nearby to
nearest regional LBS cluster
• Routes /v1/businesses writes
to Business Service primary
GDPR / CCPA Ephemeral Guard:
Never logs raw user GPS to
persistent profile storage!
2. Stateless LBS Read Path vs. Business CRUD Service
Location-Based Service (LBS) — Stateless Read-Only Fleet
Step 1: Map radius -> Geohash length (500m->L6, 2km->L5, 20km->L4)
Step 2: Compute center + 8 neighbor cells (3x3 = 9 geohash cells)
cells = [center, N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W, NW] // fixes edge split
Step 3: Parallel pipeline fetch business_ids from Geohash Cache
(Sparse rural fallback: if < K candidates at L, step to L - 1)
Step 4: Batch MGET business details from Business Info Cache
Step 5: Exact Haversine post-filter (d <= R) + sort distance ASC
Prunes 3x3 diagonal cell corners outside R (up to sqrt(2)*box)
Alt Engine: In-Memory Adaptive Point Quadtree (leaf <= 100 POIs)
~3.5-4.5 GB RAM; O(N log N) boot (2-4 min) gated by K8s /readyz;
supports native branch-and-bound k-Nearest-Neighbor (kNN) search
Business Service — CRUD & Async Index Updater
• Serves GET /v1/businesses/{id} via Business Info Valkey Cache
• Writes owner create/edit/delete to Business DB (sharded by id)
• Publishes CDC / nightly batch job to refresh Geohash cells and
build immutable Copy-on-Write Quadtree snapshots in Object Store
• Urgent closures push to Hot-Override Delta Set in < 1 second
3. Two-Tier Valkey Cache & Storage Scaling (200M POIs)
Tier 1: Geohash ID List Cache (Valkey Cluster / Replicas)
Key: "geohash:{p}:{hash}" -> Value: [biz_343, biz_347, biz_112]
• Why NOT key by raw (lat, lon)? ±10m GPS drift causes ~0% hit ratio!
• 200M POIs x 3 precisions (L=4,5,6) x ~32 B = ~19.2 GB total RAM
• Fits completely in one Valkey node's memory; replicated across AZs/regions
to scale 28.9k peak QPS without cross-shard spatial scatter-gather
Tier 2: Business Info Cache (Valkey Sharded by business_id)
Key: "business:{business_id}" -> Value: { name, lat, lon, hours, rating }
• Hydrated via single pipelined MGET for the candidate IDs in 9 cells
• Absorbs > 98% of detail reads; TTL 24h + explicit CDC invalidation
• ~200 GB raw POI corpus (~40 GB hot 20% working set in Valkey RAM)
Durable Relational / PostGIS Storage Tier
1. Business Table (~200 GB): Sharded by business_id + Read Replicas
Uniform hash distribution; zero hot-key skew across business shards
2. Geospatial Index Table (~4.8 GB raw / PostGIS GiST geometry)
Fits on a single primary + regional read replicas (NO sharding needed!)
PostGIS 3.5+: CREATE INDEX ON business USING GIST (geom) + ST_DWithin
4. Spatial Math Correctness: Why Naive 2D SQL Fails & 5-Way Index Trade-Offs
Two Bugs in Naive SQL Bounding Boxes
WHERE lat BETWEEN :lat - r AND :lat + r
AND lon BETWEEN :lon - r AND :lon + r
1. 1D B-Tree Intersection Collapse: Two 1D B-trees
scan huge global lat/lon strips and intersect O(N) rows.
2. Spherical Cosine Bug: 1 deg lon = 111.32 km * cos(lat).
At Oslo (60 deg N), cos(60) = 0.5 -> 50% E-W miss!
Fix: dLon = R / (111320 * cos(lat)) + 2D spatial index
Geohash (Morton Z-Curve) vs. Adaptive Quadtree
Geohash: 5 bits/char interleaved (even=lon, odd=lat)
• Pros: O(1) string prefix, trivial in Valkey/SQL, easy updates
• Cons: Fixed grid density; requires 9-cell query + Haversine
Quadtree: Splits NW/NE/SW/SE until leaf <= 100 POIs
• Pros: Adapts to Manhattan vs Sahara; native kNN query
• Cons: In-memory pointers; 2-4 min boot build; CoW updates
Google S2 (Hilbert) vs. Uber H3 vs. PostGIS GiST
Google S2: 6 cube faces + Hilbert curve (uint64 CellId)
• Superior spatial locality; RegionCoverer variable-level
cell coverings for arbitrary polygon geofences
Uber H3: Icosahedron hexagons (6 equidistant neighbors)
• Eliminates square sqrt(2) corner bias for surge/rings
PostGIS GiST / Valkey GEOSEARCH: Modern turnkey default
• R-tree / 52-bit geohash ZSET with built-in radius pruning
